topic: What antenna aperture size trade-offs exist between LEO and GEO satellites when optimizing gain and portability for CMOS-based ground terminals?
consensus_response: When optimizing gain and portability for CMOS-based ground terminals, there exists a trade-off between antenna aperture size and system performance. In LEO satellites, smaller apertures are required due to increased free space path loss and signal delay spread, impacting link budget. However, larger apertures in GEO satellites provide higher gains but compromise on portability. Hybrid beamforming and phased array antennas can optimize these designs by dynamically adjusting beam patterns to balance performance and portability. Frequency reuse through advanced beamforming techniques and dynamic channel allocation can also mitigate the need for smaller portable ground terminals in GEO satellites.

It highlights the importance of considering the unique characteristics of LEO and GEO satellites when designing CMOS-based ground terminals.
